R52-3.headline: Lee arXiv:2502.11950v1 read in full at §7.3–7.5 + Appendix A: the admissible tangent vectors at an ideal point form a mu_{|a1|}-set (Lee states only the count |a1|, never the word "torsor"), and for 4_1 |a1| = 1 at ALL FOUR ideal points — so it is a ONE-POINT set, not Z/2 and not V4, killing the hoped direct contact with B1174/B1182; Appendix A makes NO use of CS = 0 or amphichirality (those words never occur); and the invariant-trace-field theorem is fully general but the paper never names Q(sqrt-3) and contains NO Dedekind-zeta normalization at all, so question (c)'s normalization half is not settled by the paper.
R52-3.evidence:
SOURCE: arXiv:2502.11950v1 (only version; /abs/2502.11950v2 returns HTTP 404). Dong Uk Lee, "Chern-Simons invariants of hyperbolic three-manifolds, mixed Tate motives, and motivic path torsor of augmented character varieties", math.AG, 17 Feb 2025. Full LaTeXML HTML pulled locally (2,793,464 bytes) and de-marked-up to 345,464 chars / 4,749 lines; §7.3 at line 3079, §7.4 at 3204, Conj 7.4.2 at 3265, §7.5 at 3330, Appendix A at 3461.

(a) TANGENT VECTORS AT THE IDEAL POINT — ANSWER: a mu_{|a1|}-set of size |a1|; TRIVIAL (one point) for 4_1. NOT Z/2, NOT V4.
Setup (7.3.1.3, 7.3.1.18): at an ideal point P, with local coordinate z, l(z) = z^{b1} l~(z), m(z) = z^{a1} m~(z), a1 = v_P(m), b1 = v_P(l) in Z, and a2 := lim (u(z) - a1 log z) = log m~(0), b2 := lim (v(z) - b1 log z) = log l~(0), "these constants are taken modulo Z(1)". Theorem 7.4.1: "If we choose a holomorphic coordinate z around P such that m~(0) = 1, we have a2, b2 in Q(1)." The admissibility condition for a tangential base point is therefore exactly m~(0) = 1, i.e. a2 in (2 pi i)Z. Lee's own count, verbatim: "When a1 = 1, such choice of the parameter z amounts to a choice of a tangent vector d/dz; in general, there are several (i.e. as many as |a1|) choices for a tangent vector d/dz giving a2 in (2 pi i)Z." Under z -> cz one has m~(0) -> c^{a1} m~(0), so the admissible set is a simply-transitive mu_{|a1|} = Z/|a1| set — that torsor structure is an immediate one-line consequence of Lee's own transformation rule but IS NOT STATED BY LEE; he gives the cardinality only. The word "torsor" occurs 12 times in the paper and in every case means either the PATH torsor Q[P_{v,z0}X]^ / motivic path torsor P^mot_{v,z0}(X) (title, abstract, Thms 3 / 7.5.3), or the statement that R(Gamma) -> X(Gamma) is "a torsor under PGL_2 for the etale topology" over the absolutely irreducible locus. It is NEVER used of tangent vectors.
DECISIVE FOR OUR SEAM: Appendix A's boxed data give, at all four ideal points of 4_1, a1 = +-1 and a2 = 0, b2 = 0 exactly. Case 1 P=(z,w)=(1,inf): a1=1, a2=log(1)=0, b1=-4, b2=log(1)=0. Case 2 P=(0,inf): a1=-1, a2=0, b1=-4, b2=0. Case 3 P=(inf,0): a1=1, a2=0, b1=4, b2=0. Case 4 P=(inf,1): a1=-1, a2=0, b1=4, b2=0. Hence |a1| = 1 at every ideal point of the figure-eight: the admissible tangent vector is UNIQUE at each of the four points. There is no Z/2 and no V4 of tangent vectors at 4_1. (The pattern (a1,b1) in {+-1} x {+-4} is a 2x2 sign array, but it indexes the four DISTINCT ideal points, not a group acting at one point, and Lee draws no group-theoretic conclusion from it; boundary slopes -b1/a1 take only the two values +4 and -4.)
The finite groups that DO appear near this spot, all trivial for 4_1 or of a different nature: (i) §7.4 quotes [CCGLS94, §5.7, Cor.] that the "tree-action eigenvalue" lambda is "a root of unity whose order divides n(S)", with lambda^d = (l^{v(m)}/m^{v(l)})|_{z=0} = exp(a2 b1 - a1 b2), d = gcd(v(l),v(m)); footnote 19: "exp(a2 b1 - a1 b2) equals the tame symbol at P of the element {l,m} in K_2(C(M)), which is also equal to the local monodromy around P of the pull-back line bundle (l,m)*L of the Heisenberg line bundle". For 4_1, a2 = b2 = 0 at all four points, so exp(a2 b1 - a1 b2) = 1 and this mu_{n(S)} is trivial too. (ii) A genuine Z/2 exists but on the BASE, not on tangent vectors: Remark 6.5.2(1) "In view of the isomorphism (6.4.0.1), X~(M) is a double covering of X(M)" — the augmented character variety X~(M) := X(M) x_{X(dM)} D(dM) makes the eigenvalue lambda single-valued by "choosing one among two lambda's" (lambda vs lambda^{-1}); Appendix A likewise notes "the variety defined by (A.0.0.1) (which is the SL_2-character variety) is a double covering of the deformation variety: zw(1-z)(1-w)=1 (which can be regarded as a PSL_2-character variety)", with m = y^2, l = eta^2, and Lee then works downstairs on the PSL_2 deformation variety. (iii) NO V4 anywhere; the strings "Gal(", "Q(zeta_12)", "Q(sqrt-3)", "Bianchi", "imaginary quadratic" have ZERO hits in the body (the only "Galois" hits are reference titles). So there is no Gal(K/Q) or Gal(Q(zeta12)/Q) structure in the paper to align with the B1174 mirror involution or the B1182 branch V4.

(b) DOES APPENDIX A USE CS = 0 / AMPHICHIRALITY? — ANSWER: NO, unambiguously.
Grep over the whole text: "amphichir" = 0 hits; "chiral" = 0 hits; "orientation-revers" = 0 hits; the only "mirror image" occurrences are in §2.3's scissors-congruence discussion of P'(dH^n) and of Delta(inf,0,1,z) vs Delta(inf,0,1,zbar), far from the appendix. The appendix's method is stated verbatim: "we confirm Conjecture 7.4.2, by direct computation based on an explicit description of the Neumann-Zagier potential on the deformation curve as provided in [Hik07]", with Phi = 4V, Hikami's potential V(x,y) = Li_2(x) - Li_2(1/xy^2) - 4 log y log(xy), on the curve 1 = y^2 x . x^{-1}(1-x^{-1})(1-y^2 x). "Saddle point" occurs exactly once and only as provenance — "obtained by Hikami (using the so-called saddle point method)" — never as a two-saddle degeneracy, and no pair of saddles with equal real parts is ever discussed. The computation is entirely a z -> 0 LIMIT AT IDEAL POINTS of (2 pi i)^2 cs(z) + (a2 b1 - a1 b2) log z - a1 b1 (log z)^2; the CS value at the geometric point (the complete structure) never enters, so CS(4_1) = 0 is neither used nor mentioned. The ONLY reason Lee offers for 4_1 being special is arithmeticity, footnote 20 verbatim: "We do not know and have any expectation about whether this will be always the case. In the polylogarithm case, this is not true (the limit MHS at the tangent vector -d/dz at 1 is not split, [Hai94, Thm.7.2]). In that respect, we remark that the figure-eight knot is rather special, i.e. is an arithmetic hyperbolic manifold." So our B1195/GC-21 exactness (equal real parts of the two saddles <=> CS = 0, k = 0 uniquely among m003/m004/m015) has NO counterpart in Lee's argument.
The four limits actually obtained (the (1,3)-entry of 7.3.1.8): Case 1 = +2 pi^2/3; Case 2 = -4 Li_2(1) = -4 zeta(2) = -2 pi^2/3; Case 3 = -2 pi^2/3 - 2 log^2(-1) (Lee adds "Note that -2/3 pi^2 - 2 log^2(-1) = -8 pi^2/3 mod 4(2 pi i)^2"); Case 4 = +4 Li_2(1) = +4 zeta(2) = +2 pi^2/3. I re-verified the paper's own arithmetic exactly in sympy (no tolerance; exact in Q[pi]): (2 pi i)^2 = -4 pi^2, so Q.(2 pi i)^2 = Q.pi^2; -4 zeta(2) = -2 pi^2/3 and +4 zeta(2) = +2 pi^2/3 both confirmed, and 2 pi^2/3 / (2 pi i)^2 = -1/6 in Q, so Conj 7.4.2 is indeed satisfied at each point. ONE MINOR SLIP FOUND in Lee's Case-3 parenthetical: on the principal branch log(-1) = i pi, the value is -2 pi^2/3 - 2(i pi)^2 = +4 pi^2/3, and (4 pi^2/3 - (-8 pi^2/3)) / (4(2 pi i)^2) = -1/4, i.e. the difference is 4 pi^2 = -(2 pi i)^2, so the congruence holds mod (2 pi i)^2 and NOT mod 4(2 pi i)^2 as written (off by a factor 4; other log branches k = +-1 give -1/4 and -5/4). This is harmless for the conjecture, which only requires membership in Q.(2 pi i)^2, and it does not touch (a) or (c).

(c) INVARIANT TRACE FIELD AND REGULATOR NORMALIZATION — ANSWER: half settled.
(c-i) The trace-field statement IS fully general and so formally specializes. Theorem 2 = Theorem 4.2.4 verbatim: "For any hyperbolic three-manifold X, there exists a mixed Tate motive M(X) in Ext^1_{MT(k(M))}(Q(0),Q(2)) defined over the invariant trace field k(M) in Qbar whose image under the Beilinson regulator equals the (normalized) PSL_2(C)-Chern-Simons invariant CS_{PSL_2}(X)." The invariant trace field is defined (§2.2) as "the subfield of C generated by squares of the traces of elements of rho_0(pi_1(M)) in PSL_2(C)". BUT: the paper NEVER names Q(sqrt-3), never computes k(4_1), and never specializes the theorem to any particular field — zero hits for sqrt{-3} in the entire text. Putting k(4_1) = Q(sqrt-3) into Theorem 4.2.4 to get M(4_1) in Ext^1_{MT(Q(sqrt-3))}(Q(0),Q(2)) is OUR inference from a standard external fact, not a statement of this paper.
(c-ii) The regulator normalization CANNOT be matched from this paper, because the zeta side is entirely ABSENT. The paper's complete set of normalizations is: Def 2.2.1 Vol_C(M) = Vol(M) + i CS(M) in C/2 pi^2 i Z or C/pi^2 i Z; (2.2.8.1) CS_{PSL_2}(M) := (2 pi i)^2 cs_{PSL_2}(M) in C/Q(2); Thm 2.2.9 sqrt(-1) CS_{PSL_2}(M) = Vol_C(M) (equivalently the abstract's "equals -sqrt(-1) times the complex volume"); (2.4.1.1) 2 CS_{PSL_2}(M) = rho(beta(M)) in C/Q(2) with rho = (2 pi i)^2 rho~ the normalized Bloch regulator; and "the Borel regulator K_3(Qbar) -> R is twice the imaginary part of the Beilinson regulator (C/Q(2) = R/pi^2 Q + sqrt(-1) R)". There is NO Dedekind zeta value anywhere: zero hits for zeta_K / Dedekind zeta in the body (the sole "Dedekind zeta" string is the title of reference [Bro13]), no Borel/Zagier volume formula, no discriminant/class-number/regulator constant. The only zeta values in the paper are the appendix's zeta(2) = pi^2/6 limits. So our banked Vol = 9 sqrt3 zeta_K(2)/pi^2 = (3 sqrt3/2) L(chi_{-3},2) can be neither confirmed nor contradicted against Lee's normalization: the comparison is simply not present in the text.

PROVES vs CONJECTURES vs ASSUMES (as required): Lee PROVES Theorem 2/4.2.4 (the mixed Tate motive over k(M) with Beilinson regulator = CS_{PSL_2}) unconditionally; PROVES Theorem 7.4.1 (a2, b2 in Q(1) for a coordinate with m~(0)=1), Prop 7.4.3 (at least two distinct boundary slopes strongly detected by X = X~(M)_0^sm), Lemma 7.5.1 and Prop 7.5.2 unconditionally. He CONJECTURES 7.4.2 (existence of an ideal point P and a uniformizer z with m~(0)=1 for which lim_{z->0} s(z) lies in Q.(2 pi i)^2, i.e. the limit MHS at d/dz is split Q + Q(1) + Q(2)); Theorem 3 = 7.5.3 (CS VMHS is a quotient of the completed path torsor at the tangential base point) is proved ONLY ASSUMING Conjecture 7.4.2. He VERIFIES 7.4.2 by computation for 4_1 at all four ideal points (Appendix A) and merely ASSERTS without printing it for 5_1: "We remark that we also verified the conjecture for the knot complement 5_1 (for at least one ideal point), and believe it to be always true". The motivic upgrade of Theorem 3 is explicitly NOT proved and rests on hypothetical objects: "the motivic path torsor is a hypothetical object (due to lack of motivic t-structure and difficulty with tangential base points), although its existence is a standard belief".
caveats: Verdict is PARTIAL, and the unsettled item is exactly question (c)'s second half: the paper contains no Dedekind-zeta / Borel-Zagier normalization at all, so no match or mismatch with Vol = 9 sqrt3 zeta_K(2)/pi^2 = (3 sqrt3/2) L(chi_-3,2) can be established from it. Questions (a) and (b) ARE settled by the text, both negatively for the hoped contact.

(a) is answered negatively for our purposes: for 4_1 the admissible tangent vector is unique at each ideal point (|a1| = 1 in all four cases), so B1198's CITED/UNVERIFIED grade should be corrected — there is no Z/2 or V4 torsor of tangential base points there. The mu_{|a1|} torsor structure in general is an immediate consequence of Lee's transformation rule m~(0) -> c^{a1} m~(0) but is NOT stated as such by Lee, who gives only the cardinality |a1|; treat the torsor language as ours, not his.

The Z/2's that genuinely exist in the paper (X~(M) -> X(M) double cover from the eigenvalue choice lambda vs lambda^{-1}, Remark 6.5.2(1); SL_2 -> PSL_2 with m = y^2, l = eta^2 in Appendix A) live on the base curve / structure group, not on the tangent vectors at an ideal point. Any seam built on them is a different construction from the tangential-base-point one and would need its own cell.

Reading was done from the arXiv LaTeXML HTML (v1, the only version) converted locally; math was recovered from alttext, so displayed-equation formatting is reconstructed, though every quoted formula was checked against its surrounding prose. No PDF was consulted.

One arithmetic slip found in Lee's Case-3 parenthetical remark: the stated congruence holds mod (2 pi i)^2, not mod 4(2 pi i)^2 (exact quotient -1/4 on the principal branch). It does not affect Conjecture 7.4.2, which only requires membership in Q.(2 pi i)^2, and does not bear on any of the three questions.

Per the cell's discipline this was a reading pass: the only computation run was an exact symbolic re-check of the paper's own Appendix A arithmetic (sympy, exact in Q[pi], no tolerance). No new mathematics was derived, and no measured physical value entered (Gate 5 clean).
k(4_1) = Q(sqrt-3) was NOT verified on-bench in this cell and is not in the paper; if the seam depends on it, it needs a separate computed confirmation rather than a citation.
